reason: While Pharaoh as Egypt's leader explicitly avoids accountability (repeatedly hardening his heart and refusing to acknowledge responsibility), Moses—the leader of the Hebrew people—consistently demonstrates accountability. He repeatedly intercedes on behalf of the people before God when they complain (e.g., Exodus 15:25, 17:4), brings their grievances before the Lord, mediates disputes, and actively seeks solutions to their problems. He also accepts constructive criticism from his father-in-law Jethro and implements a better judicial system to serve the people more effectively (Exodus 18). The text shows Moses taking significant personal responsibility for the welfare of the Hebrew people throughout this passage.
